postTitle: Is 0% EMI or Buy Now Pay Later Really Free? When Free Is Free
topic: 0% instalments charge no interest, so who pays? Sometimes the shop, sometimes a higher price, sometimes a lost discount

assumptions.notes: Lesson: when a plan charges nothing, the cost lands elsewhere: the shop pays a fee (it sells more), the price is higher, or a cash discount is lost (Jiri: €1,200 in instalments or €1,140 paid now; €60, about 10% a year, left in the lesson). Free when the price is the same, no fees, every payment on time. Numbers: 0%, €1,200, €1,140.

caption.instagram:
Instalments with no interest. Who pays for that?

Sometimes the shop pays the provider a fee, because instalments help it sell more; then it can cost you nothing extra. Sometimes the cost is built into a higher price. Sometimes paying now is cheaper: a laptop at €1,200 in instalments or €1,140 paid now, and the instalments cost more, whatever the label says.

Same price, no fees, every payment on time: then it can cost you nothing extra.
